set.descent_text: The descent is long and is often the hardest part of the day. The usual way is the Crossover descent, which returns to the east-side trailhead with no car shuttle. From the summit it works down the west side of the summit ridge by cairned scrambling, a rappel from a slung block and a series of gullies and ledges (choosing the correct gully is critical) to the Slesse Mountain Trail. A cairn marks where the route leaves that trail for a notch, steep snowfields (bring an axe or at least crampons) and a contour around Mount Parkes to Crossover Pass. A rockslide damaged the old trail below the pass, so parties now rappel the bolted Crack of Noon Club route to talus, then follow cairns and flagging into the forest and rejoin the memorial trail. The alternative is the steep Slesse Mountain Trail down the west side, which ends at a different trailhead and needs a second vehicle; road access on that side has been restricted.
set.approach: Start at the Slesse Memorial trailhead on the Nesakwatch Creek forest road. The trail crosses Nesakwatch Creek on a bridge, follows an old logging road for part of the way, passes the memorial plaque and ends at the Propeller Cairn. Continue north over glacier-polished slabs, losing a little height toward a wooded ridge, and scramble a short gully (third to fourth class, often damp) to a notch in it. Drop into the cirque below the pocket glacier and climb slabs toward the head of the bowl, where the diagonal bypass ledge begins the route. Ice can fall onto these slabs from the glacier above, so cross the exposed stretch without stopping.

review.notes: Approach: route page, Abegg trip report, UBC report agree on memorial trail, Propeller Cairn, notch, cirque, bypass ledge. Descent: route page, Abegg, Haley, AAJ traverse note agree on Crossover descent; the Crack of Noon Club rappel finish after the slide is from the route and area pages. No rappel counts or times given.

set.descent_text: The route ends in heather meadows at a short wall with a bolted anchor. From there an easy scramble up and left on a cairned goat path reaches Crossover Pass, and the ridge beyond it leads west toward Slesse. To come off directly, rappel the line you climbed: every station is bolted with rings and the line is easy to follow down. The same rappels are the way down from Crossover Pass for parties returning from east-side routes on Slesse. At the bottom, cross talus, follow cairns and flagging into the forest to meet the old descent trail, and continue to the memorial trail and trailhead. Cross the slide debris near the base without stopping.
set.approach: From the Slesse Memorial trailhead, take the memorial trail to just short of the plaque, where a climbers' trail to Crossover Pass branches right. It drops to a creek, crosses on a log and climbs to a very large boulder; a newer climbers' trail turns left there and heads into the open alpine. Follow cairns and flagging to the buttress, passing flat rock slabs that make good campsites. The first pitch is on the right side of the buttress, under a bolt about 15 feet up. A band of fresh slide debris lies close to the base.

review.notes: Route page for the line, location and bolted rappel stations; Northeast Buttress page and area page confirm it is used as the descent from Crossover Pass. Distances, gain and rappel count left out (single source).

set.descent_text: The route finishes on the summit ridge, after which you cross the ridge to the high point on its north end. To descend, go back down the way you came, taking care to leave the gully at the very spot where you climbed into it. Then retrace the ledges under the west face and follow the steep climbers' trail down to the valley. Alternatively, walk off east by the standard Crossover descent.
set.approach: The usual access is the west side, from the Slesse Creek road, where a very steep climbers' trail climbs straight up to treeline. Traverse the meadowed slopes to the foot of the summit tower's west face; the best bivouac, with melt-water, is a long way below the start of the climbing. Road access in that valley has been restricted, and an alternative is to link across the mountain from the east side via the Crack of Noon Club route.

review.notes: Route page for descent by reversing, trail to treeline and meadows traverse; area page for gating of the Slesse Creek road and the Crack of Noon Club link; ACMG report for the steep west-side trail.

set.approach: The west-side approach starts on the Slesse Creek road, where a very steep climbers' trail climbs straight to treeline. Traverse the meadowed slopes toward the west face of the summit tower, then follow the scrambling route toward the southwest gully across the ledges beneath the face. The pillar starts where you have crossed most of those ledges and are about to enter the gully proper. Road access in that valley has been restricted, so check before relying on it.

review.notes: Start of the pillar relative to the southwest gully scramble from the West Pillar page; trail and meadows from the Southwest Gully page; road gating from the area page. Descent skipped (top-out not stated).

set.descent_text: The six pitches from the northern notch finish on the summit of Slesse, so the descent is the standard one. From the summit, take the standard Crossover descent. Work down the west side of the summit ridge by cairned scrambling, a short rappel from a slung block, and gullies and ledges to the Slesse Mountain Trail; picking the correct gully matters, as cliffs lie beside the wrong one. A cairn marks where the route leaves that trail for a notch, then crosses steep snow (an ice axe is useful) and contours around Mount Parkes to Crossover Pass. From the pass, rappel the bolted Crack of Noon Club route to talus, follow cairns and flagging into the forest, and rejoin the memorial trail to the east-side trailhead. A steep west-side descent to Slesse Creek also exists, but it ends far from the east-side start and road access over there has been restricted.

review.notes: Route page: six pitches from the northern notch to the summit, and standard descent marked on its photo. Standard descent details from the Northeast Buttress page and Abegg trip report. Approach skipped (only 'west side trail to the northern notch').

review.notes: Route page for the finish; Russian Roulette page for the Crossover descent after the North Rib's last pitches. Approach skipped: only 'cross the North Slesse Glacier' is given.

set.descent_text: The buttress reaches the Parkes ridge, which is followed across to join the last pitches of the North Rib on the summit of Slesse. From the summit, take the standard Crossover descent. Work down the west side of the summit ridge by cairned scrambling, a short rappel from a slung block, and gullies and ledges to the Slesse Mountain Trail; picking the correct gully matters, as cliffs lie beside the wrong one. review.notes: Route page names the Crossover pass descent after finishing on the North Rib to the summit. Approach skipped (refers to another route's approach).

The trail crosses Nesakwatch Creek on a bridge, follows an old logging road for part of the way, passes the memorial plaque and ends at the Propeller Cairn. Continue north over glacier-polished slabs, losing a little height toward a wooded ridge, and scramble a short gully (third to fourth class, often damp) to a notch in it. Drop into the cirque below the pocket glacier and climb slabs toward the head of the bowl, where the diagonal bypass ledge begins the Northeast Buttress. review.notes: Variation page: leaves the Northeast Buttress above the bivouac ledge and takes a corner to the summit. Approach and descent from the Northeast Buttress page, Abegg and UBC report.

set.descent_text: The buttress crest leads to the top of Labour Day Horn. Go down its southwest side, then contour around the south flank of the peak, cross over the south ridge, and use the lowest of three notches in the east ridge to get back onto the northeast slopes and the approach.
set.approach: Follow the Slesse Memorial Trail to the Propeller Cairn. From there, traverse south across snowpatches and slabs to the foot of the north buttress, the most prominent feature on the northeast side of Labour Day Horn.

review.notes: Route page for the traverse from the cairn and the descent; Station D page for the matching Labour Day Horn descent; traverse page for the shortest-approach remark. Times and distances left out.

set.descent_text: The route ends on the summit of Labour Day Horn. Come off by the southwest side, contour around the south flank and over the south ridge, then use the lowest of three notches in the east ridge to get back to the northeast slopes.
set.approach: Follow the Slesse Memorial Trail to the Propeller Cairn, then traverse south across snowpatches to the Labour Day Horn buttress. A long diagonal snow ramp runs beside the north buttress up to a notch behind the prominent gendarme, which is the start of the pillar.

review.notes: Route page: snow ramp to the notch and finish at the summit; descent from the Labour Day Buttress and Station D pages.

set.descent_text: From the top, go down to the basin on the south side. Then follow the Labour Day Horn descent: traverse around the south and west flanks of that peak to get back to the base of the buttress.
set.approach: Hike the Slesse Memorial Trail to the Propeller Cairn, then continue south across talus and snow beneath the Labour Day Horn buttress to Station D. The prominent buttress on that peak is the line.

review.notes: Route page for approach direction and descent; Labour Day Buttress page for its descent; AAJ for the peak order along the massif (Labour Day Horn then Station D). No times given.

set.descent_text: The traverse finishes on the main summit of Slesse. From there, descend the standard route: the Crossover descent back to the east-side trailhead, or the west-side route to Slesse Creek. Work down the west side of the summit ridge by cairned scrambling, a short rappel from a slung block, and gullies and ledges to the Slesse Mountain Trail; picking the correct gully matters, as cliffs lie beside the wrong one. A cairn marks where the route leaves that trail for a notch, then crosses steep snow (an ice axe is useful) and contours around Mount Parkes to Crossover Pass. From the pass, rappel the bolted Crack of Noon Club route to talus, follow cairns and flagging into the forest, and rejoin the memorial trail to the east-side trailhead. A steep west-side descent to Slesse Creek also exists, but it ends far from the east-side start and road access over there has been restricted.
set.approach: Take the Slesse Memorial Trail to the Propeller Cairn, then head south to Labour Day Horn, where the traverse begins. Its south ridge is the easiest way up, and the north buttress has the shortest approach.

review.notes: Traverse page: starts on Labour Day Horn by the cairn trail, ends on the main summit, standard descent to Crossover; AAJ 2018 note confirms the south-to-north order and Crossover finish.

set.descent_text: The line ends on the third peak. Go down by one of two ways: cross the west flank of the massif to join the usual descent routes, or drop into the Southeast Spur Couloir between the third and fourth peaks. Depending on the snow, the couloir can be a continuous downclimb on snow or a series of rappels over polished rock with weak anchors. Downclimbing snow is the safer choice when conditions allow.

review.notes: Single route page; no rappel count given. Approach skipped.
